ENG-04 A GUARD THAT CANNOT FIRE: assertEdgesNotStarved compares two values computed by the same predicate over the same array, before the transaction, and never against what writeAtomLinks persisted. The STARVED_EDGE control is vacuous.

ENG-02 + ENG-09 THE COLLAPSE IS COMPUTED AND DISCARDED TWICE: plan-county-owner-facts.ts:100 overwrites the loser with no count, and dedupePreparedRowsLastWins does the same at the storage layer while the caller's success count comes from the PRE-dedupe array. The write-then-verify cannot detect it, because collapsed atoms share both the PK and body.atomDid. A 1,523,640/1,523,640 verified figure is consistent with any number of collapses.
ENG-05 THE OPERATOR'S TTL DOES NOT SURVIVE: lockAndHeartbeatLease is called with no options and resets expires to DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_MS (15 min). No county writer can pass a ttlMs at all.

ENG-11 + ENG-27 HAND-DECLARED SETS: DECLARED_CAD_VINTAGES covers 15 of 254 counties (loud refusal for the other 239), and the two join-hold sets are the counties where someone noticed, never derived. ENG-27 carries the query that would derive them.

LESSON: A guard whose two operands come from the same array via the same predicate is a tautology dressed as a control. assertEdgesNotStarved is the clean instance: expectedAppliesToCount and appliesToLinkFromPropertyAtom share three skip conditions in the same order, so the check can never fire. The tell is a parameter named for a persisted count that is computed before the transaction.

A silent collapse is often ONE LINE from being measured. plan-county-owner-facts.ts:100 (out.set overwriting) and dedupePreparedRowsLastWins (byDid.set overwriting) each compute the collapse and discard it; byDid.size vs rows.length would publish it. Look for Map.set in a loop with no size comparison afterward.

A count returned to a caller and a count of rows persisted are different numbers. preparePropertyAtomRows returns `out` (pre-dedupe) and `rows` (post-dedupe), and writePropertyAtomsBatch returns `out`, so every county writer's atomsWritten overstates by exactly the collapse. The writers then ignore the return value entirely and add slice.length.

Four copies of one normalization is not redundancy, it is a divergence surface. Three JS copies agree; the fourth is SQL and has neither the all-digit guard nor the one-digit floor, so '0A123' resolves to a different parcel's geometry.

A TTL passed at take is not a TTL for the run when the heartbeat re-derives expires from a default. lockAndHeartbeatLease(sql, lease) with no options silently shortens any longer lease to 15 minutes on the first batch.
DEAD-END: A heredoc of the full register exceeded the Bash spawn argument limit on Windows (ENAMETOOLONG: uv_spawn). Large artifacts go through the Write tool, not `cat > file <<EOF`, regardless of the prefer-Bash posture.

Postgres ARE does support lookahead, but writing the normalizeForJoin equivalent as regexp_replace with (?=\d) invites a reader to doubt the equivalence. ltrim(raw,'0') plus an explicit all-zero filter is exactly equivalent over the admitted input set and is checkable by eye.
